items.q: An ad network buys ad space from publishers and resells it to advertisers.
items.why: The network bundles space from many sites and sells it as one package.

items.q: An ad network and an ad exchange are exactly the same thing.
items.why: A network buys and resells inventory itself. An exchange is an open marketplace where buyers and sellers trade in auctions.

items.q: A blind network may not tell the advertiser which sites their ads ran on.
items.why: Blind networks trade transparency for lower prices and wide reach.

items.q: A vertical ad network focuses on one kind of content or audience.
items.why: For example, a network that only sells space on travel or sports sites.

items.q: An ad network always pays publishers exactly what it charges advertisers.
items.why: The network keeps a margin, the gap between what it charges and what it pays.

items.q: Premium publishers sell only through ad networks.
items.why: Many sell directly, through private deals and through exchanges as well.
